label: S&P 500
change: +4.83% on Mon 23 Nov (about +334 points), the best day since April 2025, after Nvidia’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. It ends a seven-day losing run and recovers about half of last week’s 8.6% fall, but the index is still about 6% below its 6 Oct record. The Dow rose 3.0%
source: 24/7 Wall St closing bell 23 Nov; Yahoo Finance live 23 Nov

label: Nasdaq Composite
change: +6.46% on Mon 23 Nov (level derived from Friday’s close), its best day since April 2025. Futures tracking the Nasdaq-100 had their biggest opening jump since 1999. Small caps (Russell 2000) rose about 3%, so the rebound was broad
source: 24/7 Wall St closing bell 23 Nov; Yahoo Finance live 23 Nov

label: Semiconductor index (SOX)
change: No official index close found since 17 Nov. Chip stocks rebounded hard on Mon 23 Nov: Nvidia +31%, Micron about +19%, Dell +21%, Astera Labs +23%, Taiwan chip ADRs up 15–22% intraday, after falling about 10.7% on Fri 20 Nov
source: Nexus morning note 18 Nov; StockTitan 23 Nov; 24/7 Wall St 23 Nov

label: Nvidia after Huang’s return
change: +31.1% on Mon 23 Nov after the board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, saying government input left it confident his return poses no national security risk. One of the largest one-day gains in market value on record, but the stock is still about a third below its 6 Oct high. The independent committee investigation continues, and Reuters has reported SEC staff are examining possible accounting issues (no finding of wrongdoing)
source: 24/7 Wall St closing bell 23 Nov; StockTitan 23 Nov; Yahoo Finance live 23 Nov; Motley Fool 20 Nov (citing Reuters)

label: AMD after Nvidia’s CEO exit
change: −13.3% on Fri 20 Nov and −20.5% for the week, after short seller Hunterbrook alleged its firmware kept reaching a blacklisted Chinese server maker (AMD denies wrongdoing). A US congressman has urged scrutiny of Nvidia and AMD chip sales. Rose on Mon 23 Nov (about +4% to +8% intraday); no confirmed close found
source: Yahoo Finance live 20 Nov; TECHi 20 Nov; MarketAlleys 20 Nov; StockTitan 23 Nov

label: VIX volatility index
change: About −24% on Mon 23 Nov to about 27 (early afternoon reading; close not found), down from 38.40 on Friday but still well above calm levels

label: CoreWeave 5-yr default protection
change: No newer default-swap figure published; last reading rose as much as 76 bp to 1,233 bp on Fri 20 Nov (intraday high), below its 1,268 bp record of 5 Nov. Shares rebounded 22.4% to US$48.38 on Mon 23 Nov after −25.6% last week. AI-debt ETFs that would bet against CoreWeave, Oracle and Meta credit have been filed with the SEC
source: Le Private Banker 20 Nov (default swap data); 24/7 Wall St 23 Nov; CNBC 18 Nov

label: Oracle 5-yr default protection
change: No newer default-swap figure published; last reading about 328 bp on Fri 20 Nov, a one-month high and above the 300 bp level this watch treats as a bursting signal. Shares rose in Monday’s rebound (up about 5% before the open). Oracle reaffirmed its target of more than US$30bn of free cash flow in fiscal 2029. Rated BBB-
source: Le Private Banker 20 Nov (default swap data); 24/7 Wall St 23 Nov; Decrypt 19 Nov

label: Alphabet after its results
change: Closed −12.6% on Thu 29 Oct after its revenue and profit miss and −US$9.1bn Q3 free cash flow; ~US$280 on Fri, about 17% below a month ago
source: Saxo Options Brief 30 Oct; Yahoo Finance 30 Oct; Stocks Today 30 Oct

label: Meta equity raise
change: Largest equity raise ever, to fund AI build-out; includes preferred shares. Nvidia is investing US$3bn in it. Shares −1.6%
source: Reuters via MarketScreener; Yahoo Finance live; Kitco, 27 Oct

label: US investment-grade bond sales, 2026
change: An all-time annual record, passing 2020, driven by AI borrowing

label: US high-yield bond spread
change: 323 bp on 13 Nov, up slightly from 320 bp on 12 Nov. Broad junk bonds remain calm even as AI names swing
source: ICE BofA via MacroRadar (FRED data); CappNotes 13 Nov

label: Big-tech capex outlook
change: No hyperscaler has cut 2027 plans, but cracks are showing: analyst Ming-Chi Kuo says Google is cutting 2027 shipments of a Broadcom-designed AI chip by about a fifth (neither company has commented), and Alphabet sold bonds at wider spreads than in May. UBS estimates ~30% of expected 2028 US data-centre additions could be at risk from construction pauses. Megacaps fell 3.9% on average Fri 20 Nov (Meta −5.9%, Amazon −4.1%, Microsoft −2.8%, Alphabet −2.7%)
source: TECHi 20 Nov; GV Wire (Reuters) 5 Nov; Reuters via Yahoo Finance 4 Nov

label: US 10-yr Treasury yield
change: About +3 bp on Mon 23 Nov (early afternoon reading; close not found) as money moved back into shares, after −13 bp on Friday. 2-yr 4.63% and 30-yr 5.31% are Friday closes (no newer figures found)
source: Yahoo Finance live 23 Nov; She Who Trades 23 Nov

label: US Fed funds rate
change: A 25 bp hike on 9 Dec is about 93–96% priced (CME FedWatch, 23 Nov), down from about 100% last week. Governor Lisa Cook said waiting longer risks the Fed “getting behind the curve”. October PCE inflation and revised Q3 GDP are due 12:30am Thursday 26 Nov Melbourne time
source: FinanceFeeds 23 Nov (Reuters and Yahoo Finance citing CME FedWatch); Reuters via MarketScreener 20 Nov

label: Oil (WTI crude)
change: About −2.7% on Mon 23 Nov (January contract, early afternoon; settle not found), extending a three-week losing streak. Brent was about US$92 in early trade (US$92.57 Friday)
source: Yahoo Finance live 23 Nov; AP via BNN Bloomberg 23 Nov

label: US CPI inflation
change: October CPI +0.4% m/m (0.3% expected), core +0.3% for a third month. BLS did not publish annual rates because October 2025 data are missing. October PPI +0.3% m/m, +6.5% y/y
source: BLS release 10 Nov; StockTitan 13 Nov; Yahoo Finance 13 Nov

label: Gold

source: Yahoo Finance live 23 Nov; FinanceFeeds 23 Nov (Kitco)
